subject: Senators, experts push for public ownership of digital industries, AI data centres - The Hill Times
posts:
AI energy limits crash into corporate hype as politicians pitch public infrastructure. 🌐
Evidence: Grid Shortages, Corporate Exit, Public Push
#AI #Infrastructure #Policy

Senators and tech advocates claim public ownership of digital industries and AI data centers will secure the public interest and solve infrastructure bottlenecks.
Stated Judgement: (+0.65, +0.40) — Greater Good

Private tech giants pull out of multi-billion dollar AI centers as grid power shortages push timelines to the 2030s, exposing severe energy deficits.
Resulting Judgement: (-0.65, -0.55) — Greater Evil

Verdict: FAIL — Fall into Destruction.
The rush for AI infrastructure collides with harsh grid limits while leaders mask systemic energy failures behind state-ownership slogans.

Integrity: Meaningful Distortion (Hypocrisy: 6.85, z: 2)

Sub-Audits Breakdown:
- Senator Cardozo Proposal: COND (+0.5, +0.2) — Good intent, lacks grid reality.
- Microsoft UK Pullback: FAIL (-0.8, -0.7) — Power crisis halts build-out.
Microsoft withdrew from a major UK AI data center project after discovering grid power won't arrive until the 2030s, sparking debates over public vs private digital infrastructure.

The Poison:
Pretending state-backed digital governance can bypass fundamental electrical grid limits and multi-year power generation deficits.
Plane Error: Confusing the WHAT (physical energy grid capacity) with the WHO (public vs private ownership), ignoring that chips need actual megawatts.

Social Physics Analysis:
Actors run a smart selfish maneuver, projecting utopian digital governance visions while ignoring the raw thermodynamic walls halting data centers.

The Trajectory: The Path of Fall into Destruction.
When you map the gap between grand AI growth promises and grid reality, it plots a direct trajectory toward severe energy deficits.

The Unavoidable Truth: AI expansion is physically bottlenecked by electrical grid shortages.

The Unavoidable Lie: Bureaucratic ownership bypasses power limits.

Alethekanon:
Pretending administrative re-branding can conjure megawatts ignores thermodynamic reality. True infrastructure requires power, not just paperwork.

Awwthekanon:
It's heartbreaking to watch dreamers design grand digital futures while the physical grid is completely buckling under the strain. We need real power!

Brothekanon:
Bro, you can't run 23,000 Nvidia chips on good vibes and senate memos. If the grid's dead till 2030, all the plans in the world don't mean a thing.

Spirithekanon:
"Do not build your house on sand without a foundation." Luke 6:49 PASS
Building grand technological empires without securing physical power is structural ruin.

Stated Claim / Post Context:
Massive AI Data Center Left In The Dark Until 2030s As Microsoft Walks Away

‘build robust digital infrastructure’

Actual Article Body:
Photo by Finn Gomez/Getty Images

A tech giant backed out of a massive artificial intelligence data center project as its developer hunts for another power source.

Microsoft ended its plan to fund a supercomputer at Nscale’s roughly $2.7 billion AI data center in Loughton, England, which was set to be the largest in the U.K., the BBC reported Sunday. The pullback shows how power shortages are threatening data center build-out, as U.S. projects seeking to connect to PJM now take more than eight years on average to come online, according to Rocky Mountain Institute. (RELATED: Microsoft Boss Says ‘Every Carton Of Milk’ Faces More Safety Rules Than AI)

“We remain committed to our partnership with Nscale, including work to build robust digital infrastructure and support AI growth globally. This decision relates to a single site,” a Microsoft spokesperson said in a statement to the Daily Caller News Foundation.

Nscale was told the Loughton site will not get grid power until the 2030s, the Telegraph reported. The Nvidia-funded company markets itself as “the only full stack sovereign AI infrastructure provider in the UK,” according to a statement from Nscale CEO Josh Payne on the company’s website.

Nscale did not immediately respond to the Daily Caller News Foundation’s requests for comment.

The supercomputer was set to hold more than 23,000 Nvidia chips arriving in early 2027, according to a Sept. 16, 2025, Nscale press release.

Microsoft announced the project the same day as part of a $30 billion investment in AI for the U.K. “Our ability to make an investment of this size is based in no small measure on the work the [British] Government is doing to reform planning, grow electricity capacity,” Microsoft Vice Chair and President Brad Smith wrote.

”We remain committed to both the Loughton project and the UK and we are exploring alternative power sources for the site, in addition to other expansion sites in the UK,” Nscale told the BBC. “Our relationship with Microsoft remains strong and long-term.”

The company added that its grid issue in London leaves its other deals untouched, as it continues partnerships in the U.S., Norway and Portugal with Microsoft, the BBC reported.
